reason: The hypothesis directly restates the well-known mechanism from P1 and P3 that a protective Cr2O3 and spinel oxide layer forms on FeCoNiMnCu coatings at high temperature and enhances wear resistance, and it applies this to the same alloy system (FeNiCrCoCu) without introducing a new material, regime, or mechanistic link. The proposed pre-oxidation intervention is a trivial variation of the thermal exposure already studied in P1 and P3, merely shifting the oxide formation to before wear testing.
copied_elements: protective oxide scale (Cr2O3, spinel) formation on FeCoNiMnCu coating at high temperature (P1, P3)
oxide layer reduces wear by acting as a barrier (P1, P12, P23, P32)
high-temperature wear resistance improves due to oxide film (P11, P12, P23, P32)
